items.title: Burrill Crohn interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, January 3, 2012
items.q: I remember going to 52nd Street and hearing Wilbur and Sidney DeParis.

ctx.x: Yes. I mean as soon as I was old enough to get into a club, and even when I couldn’t. Yeah I was lucky. I grew up in New York. I was born in Paris but I moved when I was

very young, and there was jazz everywhere in New York back then. And my early taste was to swing, because the people I listened to were the big bands and Harry James. I remember finding an early recording of Harry James where he played a great recording. He played in a small group in Chicago. It was unbelievable, that small group stuff. And I remember going to 52nd Street and hearing Wilbur and Sidney DeParis. You know who they are. And then, but then I heard Roy Eldridge and I actually heard Bird before he died,…
Can you recall, at the time, however old you were, were you aware that you were listening to legendary people?
